name: Vikunja
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Vikunja is a self-hosted to-do app for tasks and projects, with lists, kanban boards and CalDAV. Sign-ups stay closed unless you open them; the first account comes from the server's settings.
startup: export VIKUNJA_SERVICE_INTERFACE=":{{SERVER_PORT}}"; if [ "{{OPEN_SIGNUPS}}" = 1 ]; then export VIKUNJA_SERVICE_ENABLEREGISTRATION=true; else export VIKUNJA_SERVICE_ENABLEREGISTRATION=false; fi; unset VIKUNJA_SERVICE_PUBLICURL VIKUNJA_CORS_ENABLE; if [ -n "{{PUBLIC_URL}}" ]; then export VIKUNJA_SERVICE_PUBLICURL="{{PUBLIC_URL}}"; else export VIKUNJA_CORS_ENABLE=false; fi; if [ -n "{{ADMIN_USERNAME}}" ] && [ -n "{{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}" ] && [ ! -f .raptor-first-user ]; then ./vikunja user create -u "{{ADMIN_USERNAME}}" -e "{{ADMIN_EMAIL}}" -p "{{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}" && touch .raptor-first-user || echo "The first account wasn't created (it may already exist)."; fi; exec ./vikunja

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Vikunja: downloads Vikunja (with its web interface built in) from its
# GitHub releases, checked against GitHub's and Vikunja's SHA-256, and
# writes a first config.yml with a secret of its own. The database,
# attachments and an existing config.yml are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Vikunja has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$want" = latest ] || want="v${want#v}"
tag=$(gh-release tag go-vikunja/vikunja "$want") || fail "Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 2.8.0, then reinstall."

if [ -x vikunja ] && [ "$(cat .vikunja-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Vikunja $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Vikunja $tag"
    bin="vikunja-$tag-linux-$arch"
    gh-release download go-vikunja/vikunja "$tag" "$bin-full.zip" "$work/vikunja.zip"
    unzip -qo "$work/vikunja.zip" -d "$work/v"
    [ "$(sha256sum "$work/v/$bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$work/v/$bin.sha256")" ] ||
        fail "The download didn't match Vikunja's checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    install -m 0755 "$work/v/$bin" vikunja.new
    mv -f vikunja.new vikunja
    echo "$tag" > .vikunja-version
fi

mkdir -p files
# A first configuration: SQLite in the server's folder and a secret for
# sign-ins made here, so sessions survive restarts. The port, sign-ups
# and address come from the server's settings at every start.
if [ ! -f config.yml ]; then
    secret=$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=\n' | head -c 48)
    cat > config.yml <<YAML
# Vikunja's settings: https://vikunja.io/docs/config-options
service:
  secret: "$secret"
  rootpath: "/home/container"
  timezone: "UTC"
database:
  type: "sqlite"
  path: "/home/container/vikunja.db"
files:
  basepath: "/home/container/files"
sentry:
  enabled: false
  frontendenabled: false
YAML
    chmod 600 config.yml
    echo "Wrote a first config.yml."
fi
echo "Installed Vikunja $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Vikunja version to install, such as 2.8.0, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: First username
variables.description: The username of the first account, created at the next start with First email and First password.

variables.name: First password
variables.description: The first account's password (at least 8 characters). Change it in Vikunja afterwards; this is used only once.

variables.name: Open sign-ups
variables.description: Let anyone who can reach the server make an account.

variables.name: Address
variables.description: The full public address of Vikunja, starting with http or https, used in emails and links. Needed for the desktop app; leave it empty to use the address it's opened at.
